id_routing.description: Interconnect may append bits to AxID to identify the originating master; slave-side ID_WIDTH > master-side ID_WIDTH
id_routing.compliance_note: Returning ID is the WIDER value; routing strips appended bits before returning to the master

fields.topology_type: Point-to-point single-host / single-device differential serial link per SATA port. Up to 32 ports per AHCI HBA, each independent. Each port can optionally fan out to up to 15 SATA devices via a Port Multiplier (PM). There is no shared-medium 'bus' anywhere in the fabric.

supported_topologies.name: Single port + single SATA device
supported_topologies.description: Most common: one HBA port → one HDD/SSD/ATAPI.

supported_topologies.name: Tiered AHCI + Bridge
supported_topologies.description: AHCI HBA + PCI-to-PCI bridge + second AHCI HBA + PM.

fields.interconnect_role: AHCI defines no protocol-level router. Each SATA link is independent and dedicated. Port Multipliers operate at the FIS level.

ordering_guarantees.within_a_fis: Dwords transmitted in strict order; SOF/EOF/CRC framing.
ordering_guarantees.across_commands_ncq: NCQ may complete out-of-order via Set Device Bits FIS.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: AHCI registers occupy non-cacheable memory behind ABAR (BAR5). System memory carries Command List / Command Tables / PRDs / Received FIS Structures.
default_signal_values_evidence_tables: Figure 3 — Example of HBA Silicon Supporting Both Legacy and AHCI Interfaces
